cells.tense: You are here, in the finished thing, with the pen still in your hand.
cells.act: draw the shape of it without the details
cells.ask: Take the last few times something in your life ended and draw the shape they share — no names, no story, just the line that runs through all of them.
cells.core:
What's finishing now is finishing cleanly. Some part of your life is ending, and you're not dragging it out or pretending it isn't happening — the clearing is going on and you're in it, awake. That's why there's no noise around it. You can be in something that's over without it being a loss, and that's no small thing. It's the work of this hour.

What carries you is seeing the pattern under the endings. Not this ending, the shape of them — what keeps arriving when one thing closes. Take the last few times something in your life ended and draw the shape they share, no names, no story, just the line that runs through all of them. Then let the clearing keep going. You'll know the next thing by its shape before it even arrives.
cells.sheetLine: Something's ending cleanly, and you're awake for it.
cells.place: at the finish, clearing for what comes next

cells.tense: Tomorrow's clearing is already done in your head, and today is a waiting room.
cells.act: leave it undecided a while longer
cells.ask: Leave the next thing undecided for one more day. Don't pick the ending, don't pick the replacement — let both sit open until tomorrow's version of this shows up.
cells.core:
You're shining ahead of where you stand. Something is finishing, and you've already got the next chapter cast, produced, and lit — you're selling tickets to a room nobody's built yet. That's the shine outrunning the thing it's shining for, and it's why the ones beside you squint. What you are isn't something to launch. It's something to become, and becoming waits for the room it's in.

So leave the next thing undecided for one more day. Don't pick the ending, don't pick the replacement. Let both sit open until tomorrow's version of this shows up — because it will, and it won't look anything like today's. Meet this moment as a stranger, not as a launch. The light lands on what's actually here instead of on the distance, and the squinting stops. The ending will still be there tomorrow. Your version of it probably won't.
cells.sheetLine: You've lit the next room before this one is cleared.
cells.place: at the finish, clearing for what comes next

cells.tense: You are still standing at a door that closed behind you some time back.
cells.act: choose this, not that, and mean it
cells.ask: Choose between two things in the clearing — keep this, let that go — and don't soften either side. One sentence, written down is fine.
cells.core:
Something in you finished, and you haven't let that count. You know how it looked when it was on — and you've been standing sideways to it, saying it was nothing, that you had help, that it wasn't as much as it seemed. The light didn't go out. You turned away from it, and the clearing has stalled while you do.

So choose between two things in the clearing, this and not that, and don't soften either side. One sentence, written down is fine. You don't have to get the ending right or justify it. You just have to point at one of them and mean it — the same way you once pointed at what you were making and meant it. That's how a light that's been turned down comes back up: a choice gets made, and the making is yours.
cells.sheetLine: You finished something real, and you've been calling it nothing.
cells.place: at the finish, clearing for what comes next

cells.tense: You are in a room you're already writing, with the pen set down.
cells.act: meet what is arriving as it arrives
cells.ask: Whatever arrives today — a message, a mood, a knock — meet it as this moment's entry, not as more of yesterday. Nothing to brace against. Just the thing as it comes.
cells.core:
Something is ending and something is arriving in the same breath, and you're meeting it without noticing that's what you're doing. You keep calling it getting through the day. What's actually happening is a turning — old ground clearing, new ground landing — and it turns around where you stand. The shine is going out of you into whatever you touch, and you haven't claimed it as yours yet.

Whatever arrives today, meet it as this moment's entry, not as more of yesterday. Nothing to brace against. A message, a mood, a knock at the door — take it as it comes, on time, not early and not late. This is already what you do. Naming it changes nothing except that it becomes yours to do on purpose — and a turning you're steering beats a turning you're surviving.
cells.sheetLine: You're the turning, not the person it happens to.
cells.place: at the finish, clearing for what comes next
